-- Authored template CSS is developer-authored; the library does not sanitize it on the author's behalf. Interpolated `${...}` values can carry runtime data, so three structural guards stop an untrusted value from escaping its context: interpolation-slot realization in `parser/compile.ts` (a slot cannot introduce new declarations or rules, or leave a comment, string, paren, or bracket open), the SSR style-body escaping in `utils/escapeStyleSink.ts` (a value cannot close the `<style>` tag), and React's own DOM-attribute escaping for everything routed through `createElement`. Preserve all three when touching those paths; each has a regression test.

+- Authored template CSS is developer-authored; the library does not sanitize it on the author's behalf. Interpolated `${...}` values and style-object values can carry runtime data; a style object's keys read as authored text. A value holds `property: value;` declarations or whole rules: on a component it can add declarations, rules composed from the component's class (a selector such as `:not(&)` reaches outside it, as it would in authored CSS), and unscoped at-rules such as `@import`, `@font-face`, and `@keyframes`; in `createGlobalStyle`, where nothing scopes a rule, it can add any whole rule. It cannot change the blocks the template wrote. A paren, string, or bracket a value opens can close later in its statement; one the template opens must close in the template. Four structural guards hold this: `fillAst` in `parser/compile.ts` (a template's blocks come from its authored text alone, and a value that cannot stay in its field is parsed on its own, with `wholeStatements` in `parser/parser.ts` dropping what it leaves unmatched or open, and warning in development), `wholeRule` and `formatDecl` in `parser/emit-web.ts` (every emitted head and every plugin rewrite is read again, since joining and plugins write text after its parts were read; a rule holding the separator or starting with a group marker is dropped, since rehydration reads server-rendered text through an HTML parser and a trim; composed selector text is bounded), the SSR style-body escaping in `utils/escapeStyleSink.ts` (a value cannot close the `<style>` tag), and React's own escaping of `<style>` text and attributes for everything routed through `createElement`. Text rewritten after those guards must leave a url token alone, as `wrapLevelInWhere` in `models/StyledComponent.ts` does: a `(` written inside one ends it early. Preserve all four when touching those paths; the first three have regression tests.

- `scanQPB` must tokenize strings, blocks, and url tokens the way a browser does: a `}` it reads as inside a string but a browser does not reaches server-rendered `<style>` text as a real close, and the text after it becomes a global rule. `url(a'b)` is one token ending at the first `)`, and a name holding an escape, or `url` straight after `&`, might mean `url`, so it counts as left open where the two readings differ; a raw newline ends a string; only a block's mirror closes it. Guarded by "keeps rules inside the scope past a bad url" and "emits nothing for %s, which a browser reads past its statement" in `compiler.test.ts`.

- The in-house parser and the native transform regexes run on user-influenced input, so they must stay linear-time. Never write a regex that can backtrack catastrophically: no `\s` inside a quantified class flanked by outer `\s*`, no lazy `[^X]+?` with a trailing `\s*`, no adjacent greedy-then-lazy `[^{}]` runs across a delimiter. Prefer `indexOf` plus anchored single-pass scanning over nested quantifiers, and give any hot-path regex a wall-clock-budget regression test.
